title: Latency and Cost Engineering: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Latency and Cost Engineering: Visual Guide

1. Budget Becomes Bill | the context-budgeting dial from the earlier lesson re-priced: a chunks-in-prompt slider and a query-rate switch turning 10 chunks x 500 tokens into 500 million input tokens a day | input tokens are the dominant variable cost, so a per-query saving only matters once you multiply it by the query rate, and eight focused chunks beat fifteen loose ones on both cost and quality

2. The Pre-Generation Wall | a p50/p95 waterfall over rewrite, retrieval, rerank, assembly and time-to-first-token with toggles for each, plus an output-token slider driving decode | streaming hides decode but never the pre-generation block, which must fit in roughly two seconds; budget with the sum of stage p95s and verify against the measured end-to-end p95

3. Where Caches Cut In | the five-stage chain with embedding, result and answer caches showing which stages each one skips, a hit-rate slider converting to executions eliminated per day, and a semantic-key toggle | savings and danger rise together along the chain, the result cache is usually the highest-value layer, and semantic keys raise hit rate by answering questions the user did not ask

4. What The Key Carries | six togglable key components (model version, index generation, tenant + ACL hash, corpus generation, prompt version, TTL) building a cache key, each one off revealing the failure it prevented | a cache never needs clearing if its key already names everything that can invalidate it, and an ACL-blind result key is a cross-tenant leak

5. Stuff It Or Search It | stuffed-context size and query rate driving daily input tokens on both paths, with three real workloads that resolve to retrieval, long context, or both | retrieval pays the corpus cost once at ingest while long context pays it every query, so bigger windows move the break-even point rather than repealing it
